title: Find the Number of Subsequences With Equal GCD
summary: Given an integer array, determine the count of distinct pairs of non-overlapping subsequences where the GCD of elements in each subsequence is identical.
statement: Given an integer array, determine the count of distinct pairs of non-overlapping subsequences where the GCD of elements in each subsequence is identical. Return the count modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Assign indices to two ordered, nonempty, disjoint subsequences or to neither; subsequence order follows nums.
Count assignments whose two subsequence GCDs are equal, modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Each index has three disjoint choices: unused, first subsequence, or second subsequence.
Aggregate prefixes by the pair of GCDs produced so far, using zero as the empty identity.
Copy states for unused; add transitions gcd(first,x) and gcd(second,x); sum equal nonzero pairs.
The three transitions are exhaustive and mutually exclusive, while the state retains exactly what future GCD updates need.
editorial: The three transitions are exhaustive and mutually exclusive, while the state retains exactly what future GCD updates need.

tests.explanation: Ten ordered disjoint subsequence pairs have equal GCD one.
The two valid ordered pairs swap [10] and [20,30], both with GCD ten.
